title: Check: Area of Parallelograms and Trapeziums

questions.stem: What is the area of a parallelogram with base $9\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $4\text{ cm}$?
questions.explanation: Area of a parallelogram $= b \times h = 9 \times 4 = 36\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.stem: A trapezium has parallel sides of $6\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$, and a perpendicular height of $5\text{ cm}$. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a trapezium $= \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h = \frac{1}{2}(6 + 10) \times 5 = \frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times 5 = 40\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.stem: Which formula correctly gives the area of a trapezium with parallel sides $a$ and $b$ and height $h$?
questions.explanation: The area of a trapezium is $\frac{1}{2}(a + b)h$, where $a$ and $b$ are the parallel sides and $h$ is the perpendicular height.
